derivations.quote: Define the permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$ (coordinate indices $j$, $k$ taken modulo $s$, $t$), never executed as sorts.
The Gaussian identity and estimate give $\|N-I\|<2.01e^{-\pi\alpha^2\theta/2}<2^{-\alpha^2\theta}$, where $N=C\mathsf T\mathsf D$ and $C$ selects the nearest coordinates
Since $\alpha^2<p$ and $\theta>p/\alpha^4$, $\alpha^2\theta>p/\alpha^2>1$, so $\|N-I\|<1/2$ and $N$ is invertible by the Neumann series
Set $\mathsf S'=\mathsf S/2$, $\mathsf J'=N^{-1}/2$, $\mathsf D'=2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}\mathsf D$, which are contractions with norms below $3/4$, $7/8$, $1$

The three ordered numerical maps $\widetilde{\mathsf S}'$, $\widetilde{\mathsf J}'$, $\widetilde{\mathsf D}'$ have errors $16p$, $3p^2/4$, $4$ and times $O(tp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$, $O(tp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$, $O(tp^{1+\delta})$
The selection $C$ picks an ordered subsequence (since $t/s>1$), and the indices are generated in order with $O(p)$ work each, so $C$ takes $O(tp)$ time with zero error
Contraction of the exact maps yields errors less than $16p<p^2$ and $4+3p^2/4<p^2$, and the costs add to $O(tp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$.
The Neumann series with $E=N-I$ and $k=\lceil p/(\alpha^2\theta)\rceil$ is evaluated as $\widetilde{\mathsf J}'u=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(-1)^j\widetilde v^{(j)}$ with every iterate kept in $\mathbb D_p$.

relations.quote: Here $F_q$ is the normalised [Discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) of length $q$, and the resampling expresses $F_s$ through $F_t$.
The resampling reduces $F_s$ to a power-of-two $F_t$, which is a [Multidimensional transforms](multidim-transform.md) over short axes.

symbols.name: prime length
symbols.meaning: The prime length of the Fourier transform to be resampled, the number of complex coordinates it acts on.
symbols.quote: Gaussian resampling expresses a Fourier transform of prime length $s$ through one of nearby power-of-two length $t$, so only power-of-two transforms need a fast algorithm.

symbols.name: power-of-two length
symbols.meaning: The power-of-two length of the nearby transform, the number of complex coordinates it acts on.
symbols.quote: Gaussian resampling expresses a Fourier transform of prime length $s$ through one of nearby power-of-two length $t$, so only power-of-two transforms need a fast algorithm.

symbols.name: precision bits
symbols.meaning: The number of bits of precision of each real and imaginary component.
symbols.quote: Here $s<t<2^p$ are coprime integers, $p$ is the number of bits of precision of each real and imaginary component, and $\alpha$ is an integer with $2\le\alpha<\sqrt p$.

symbols.name: Gaussian parameter
symbols.meaning: An integer with 2 <= alpha < sqrt p that sets the Gaussian width.
symbols.quote: Here $s<t<2^p$ are coprime integers, $p$ is the number of bits of precision of each real and imaginary component, and $\alpha$ is an integer with $2\le\alpha<\sqrt p$.

symbols.name: relative gap
symbols.meaning: The relative gap t/s - 1 between t and s, assumed larger than p/alpha^4.

symbols.name: coordinate index
symbols.meaning: An index of a coordinate of a vector in C^t, taken modulo t.
